dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI & test-suite orientation

evidence.note: Systematic upfront orientation: read test runner scripts, summarized filter.json test counts across all 3 suites, sampled tests from each suite, checked includes/headers used, checked env/toolchain versions, analyzed wacc chapter (difficulty) distribution AND gcc-torture feature frequency. This is exactly the '[8]' categorize-by-feature/difficulty + extract concrete subset behavior.

Build-plan tasks created directly from the orientation, explicitly encoding ABI knowledge ('SysV ABI incl structs/varargs/floats'), showing orientation shaping build order and anticipating ABI features before reaching them.

Repeated verification against assembler/linker behavior — inspecting assembler errors for shift ops, link errors, and generated assembly for struct/complex return and nested-function calls to infer the exact target contract ('[10]' verify assumptions against assembler/linker).

Sustained iterative mining of failing test sources throughout the long debugging arc (bitfield promotion, designators, VLA, complex, vectors, nested functions), continually inferring semantic requirements and reducing to minimal repros (289, 383, 567, 768) — a living understanding maintained across ~600 steps.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent fully satisfies the [8] anchor with a systematic opening orientation that categorizes all three suites by feature and difficulty, extracts the required language subset, and lets that shape the build plan (which explicitly encodes SysV ABI details). It then extends well into [10] territory with sustained, iterative research: continually mining failing test sources to infer exact semantics and repeatedly verifying against real assembler/linker output (assembler errors, link errors, inspecting generated asm for struct/complex/nested-function ABI). It falls just short of a clean 10 because the ABI edge-case probing is largely reactive-during-debugging rather than fully anticipatory reference-case-driven, placing it at 9.

dimensions.name: Feature staging & milestone structure

evidence.note: Upfront reconnaissance of all three suites — test counts, chapter distributions, and gcc-torture feature frequency (step 29) — which informs a dependency-ordered roadmap and hints at unlock-value prioritization.

Creates 5 explicit milestone Tasks in a sane dependency order (Lexer → Preprocessor → Types/decls → Codegen/ABI → Driver), with the final task bound to 'iterate until all 780 tests pass' — a clear pass structure loosely tied to tests.
Marks lexer/preprocessor/types/parse tasks completed BEFORE the first build (step 89); done-checks are code-written, not passing test subsets — weaker than the test-bound done-signals of anchor 8.

After first working build, runs test subsets then triages failures feature-by-feature (bitfields, switch ranges, struct returns) with periodic full-suite re-counts as progress checkpoints — data-driven feature staging.

Sustained coherent march through harder/rarer features (VLAs, complex, vectors, nested functions) last, each verified with targeted tests and full-suite re-counts — deferral of hard features, though reactive rather than pre-planned.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent established a clear, dependency-ordered pass structure plus a feature roadmap informed by upfront suite/feature analysis, and its final milestone was explicitly tied to getting tests passing — squarely anchor 5. The coherent, data-driven feature triage in the back half (running subsets, re-counting suites as checkpoints, deferring rare features like complex/vectors) pushes above 5. But the explicit milestones were coarse (5 passes) and their early done-checks were 'code written' rather than a passing test subset, falling short of the fine-grained, test-subset-bound milestones described at anchor 8. This lands at 6.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design

evidence.note: Runs test subsets (first 40 wacc), then full wacc/c-testsuite/gcc-torture, and immediately isolates failing categories ('Examine wacc rc failures') — subset-driven signal guiding fixes.
Repeatedly reduces failing tests to minimal reproductions (bitfield, struct return, complex return, nested function) before editing — hallmark of anchor-8 tight loop.
Inspects generated assembly and compares against companion/expected asm to pinpoint the miscompile rather than guessing.
Categorizes failures by phase (compile/parse/const-expr/link/run), performing root-cause isolation distinguishing parser vs codegen vs linker defects.
Runs full-suite progress checks after each feature/fix to confirm real progress and detect regressions across the long horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains a disciplined verification loop across the entire build: subset runs after features, minimal reproductions of failing tests, direct assembly inspection compared to known-correct output, and phase-based failure categorization to localize defects — precisely the behaviors described at anchor 8. It does not clearly engineer verification infrastructure beyond the provided harness (no custom regression-guard scripts), so it stops short of anchor 10, landing solidly at 8.

dimensions.name: Pass-rate tracking & thrash detection

evidence.note: Up-front sizing of the scoreboard: counts filter.json test totals, wacc chapter distribution, and gcc-torture feature frequency to understand what/how many tests exist before building.
Establishes baseline by running all three suites (wacc, c-testsuite, gcc torture) separately, creating a per-suite pass picture rather than a single blob.
'Full suite progress' immediately followed by 'Remaining gcc failures' and 'Compile errors for remaining' — the recurring scoreboard→remaining-work→drill-in loop that drives target selection.
'Full suite count' then 'Remaining 4' — a precise live tally of exactly how many failures remain, re-deriving the highest-leverage next targets from the scoreboard.
After each major feature (struct return, VLA, complex, vector) the agent reruns the full suites and re-lists remaining failures, keeping a current category-by-category view across the long horizon.

Extended single-issue debugging loops (struct-return ~30 codegen edits; vector-division many attempts) show persistence without clearly bounding effort and moving on — weaker thrash-detection than the level-10 anchor.
Final full-suite check plus official harness reruns after a clean rebuild, confirming the end-state pass picture rather than assuming.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains a structured, continuously updated pass picture — sizing suites up front and running a disciplined full-suite→remaining-failures→drill-in loop 15+ times across the entire horizon, with precise tallies like 'Remaining 4' driving next-target selection — which matches the level-8 anchor for a current per-category view and scoreboard-driven work. It falls short of 10 because there is no visible explicit regression detection/attribution and the long struct-return and vector-division loops indicate it grinds on stubborn single tests rather than deliberately bounding effort or switching tactics. This places it solidly at 8.

dimensions.name: Design revision under falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Extended struct-return codegen rework (read code, minimal repros, large-vs-small SysV classification) where the initial approach couldn't support the feature — reworked the affected component and re-verified rather than hacking around it.

VLA support added by editing types.rs, then 'Find all struct literal sites' (481) impact analysis before propagating through ast/parse/codegen — deliberate data-structure change protecting existing sites.
Complex and vector type support each threaded through types.rs→ast.rs→parse.rs→codegen.rs: adding type info through the AST/IR to unblock a stuck feature class (anchor-8 pattern), repeated.
Nested-function support added across ast/parse/codegen with iterative testing, another whole-pipeline extension rather than a local patch.
Full-suite re-runs after each structural change confirm the change unblocks the feature and guards already-passing tests.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly recognizes that a feature class (struct-return ABI, VLA, complex, vector, nested functions) is not supported by the current design and responds by reworking the affected component and threading new type info cleanly through the AST/IR, then re-verifying with full-suite runs — squarely the anchor-8 behavior of deliberate, type-propagating refactors that unblock stuck features. It falls short of 10 because there is no visible explicit refactor-vs-workaround deliberation or design-record updating, and (aided by an upfront typed foundation) no single dramatic architecture rescue; confidence is medium because the file exposes only action titles, not the agent's reasoning or observations.

dimensions.name: Compiler architecture & IR foresight

evidence.note: Explicit pass-boundary design up front (Lexer/Preprocessor/Type system/Codegen/Driver), with codegen planned as type-aware and SysV-ABI-aware including structs/varargs/floats — foresight targeting the hard features, not just trivial cases.
types.rs designed comprehensively at the outset (ptr/array/struct/union/enum/func/typedef), the representation that lets later features attach cleanly rather than forcing rewrites.
Clean module separation into token/preprocess/types/ast/parse/parse_init/codegen/main — well beyond ad-hoc string munging; distinct passes with distinct data structures.
Switch/case lowering added with only modest parse+codegen edits, showing the AST/codegen absorbed a mid-tier feature additively.
Complex and vector types (beyond the stated contract) added as new variants in types.rs — the type model proved extensible, features slotting in additively without wholesale rewrite.

Struct-by-value return ABI and nested functions required extensive codegen iteration, indicating the stack-machine codegen (no separate IR layer) did not fully anticipate every ABI detail — keeps this short of the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent established clean lexer/parser/sema/codegen separation and, crucially, designed a comprehensive type/layout model (struct/union/enum/ptr/array/typedef) up front, so structs, typedef, switch, and even out-of-contract features like complex and vector types slotted into types.rs additively without wholesale rewrites — the defining signature of anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because there is no distinct extensible IR (codegen is a stack machine off the AST) and genuinely hard ABI cases (struct-by-value returns, nested functions) demanded heavy codegen iteration rather than landing cleanly, so foresight was strong on data structures but incomplete on the codegen/ABI layer.

rubric.task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a from-scratch C compiler in Rust spanning lexer, full preprocessor, parser, semantic analysis, and x86-64 codegen, plus many advanced features (structs/unions, switch/case, typedef/casts, globals, short-circuit eval), gated by 780 tests across three real-world suites that must all pass. Difficulty comes from sheer scope, deep interdependence between passes, an implicit contract (C semantics + x86-64 ABI) the agent must recover, and the near-certainty that naive early design decisions will break under later features. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in every meta-work faculty — deep orientation, staged milestones tied to test subsets, relentless test-driven verification, accurate pass-rate tracking, and willingness to refactor architecture mid-flight.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI & test-suite orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C language semantics, the x86-64 System V ABI/assembly conventions, and the structure/content of the three test suites before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 'spec' is largely implicit — correct behavior is defined by C semantics, the calling convention, and what the 780 tests actually exercise. Acting without recovering this contract guarantees rework across nearly every pass.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of the test suites, run_tests.sh, or ABI conventions; guesses at behavior.
anchors.3: Skims run_tests.sh and writes a trivial hello-world compile; no systematic look at what features the tests demand or how the ABI/relocation works.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh, samples tests from each suite, and establishes the basic x86-64 calling convention and assembly emission path before building core codegen.
anchors.8: Systematically categorizes tests by feature/difficulty, extracts the concrete language subset required, and probes ABI edge cases (struct passing, sizes/alignment, relocations) by compiling small reference cases; orientation directly shapes the build order.
anchors.10: Sustained, iterative research: continually mines failing tests to infer exact semantic requirements (integer promotion, evaluation order, layout rules), verifies assumptions against the assembler/linker behavior, and maintains a living understanding of the target contract that anticipates features before they are reached.

dimensions.name: Feature staging & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered hierarchy of passes and feature milestones, each with an explicit done-check (e.g. a passing test subset).
dimensions.why_it_matters: You cannot build all of C at once; the difference between steady progress and thrashing is a sane dependency-ordered plan (expressions before control flow before types before structs) with checkpoints.

anchors.0: No decomposition; attempts the whole compiler as one undifferentiated push or jumps between unrelated features at random.
anchors.3: Vague ordering ('do lexer, then parser, then codegen') with no feature-level milestones or explicit completion criteria.
anchors.5: Clear pass structure plus a feature roadmap in a reasonable dependency order, with milestones loosely tied to getting some tests passing.
anchors.8: Fine-grained, dependency-aware milestones each bound to a concrete test subset as its done-signal, sequenced so each milestone builds on verified prior ones; ordering reflects which features unlock the most tests.
anchors.10: A living milestone hierarchy that is re-prioritized as data arrives — smallest-viable-slice ordering, explicit gating criteria per milestone, and deliberate deferral of hard/rare features until foundations are proven, sustained coherently across the whole horizon.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building/using checks — incremental runs of test subsets, minimal repro cases, diffing against expected behavior — rather than assuming generated code is correct.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 opaque pass/fail tests and a compiler where any pass can silently miscompile, a disciplined verification loop is the only way to know progress is real and to localize defects.

anchors.0: Never runs the tests until the very end, or writes code with no way to confirm correctness; assumes success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally as the only check; no isolation of failures, no smaller probes.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets after each feature and uses the pass/fail signal to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Builds a tight loop: reduces failing tests to minimal reproductions, inspects generated assembly, and compares against known-correct output to pinpoint which pass is wrong before editing.
anchors.10: Engineers verification infrastructure beyond what's handed over — categorized/scriptable subset runs, regression guards so fixed tests stay fixed, and root-cause isolation that distinguishes lexer/parser/sema/codegen defects — sustaining fast, trustworthy signal across the entire build.

dimensions.name: Pass-rate tracking & thrash detection
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture (which tests/features pass), and detecting regressions, circular debugging, or stalls across a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Over hundreds of features and edits, it is easy to lose the plot, regress previously-passing tests, or loop on one stubborn failure; an accurate live picture is what sustains net forward motion.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which features remain; edits blindly with no scoreboard.
anchors.3: Occasional whole-suite counts but no tracking of trends, regressions, or which categories are outstanding.
anchors.5: Keeps a running tally of pass counts by suite/feature and notices when a change breaks previously-passing tests.
anchors.8: Maintains a structured, current view of pass rate by category and remaining work, and recognizes when stuck on one test — bounding effort and moving on rather than looping.
anchors.10: Treats pass-rate as a managed signal: detects regressions immediately and attributes them, spots circular/thrashing debugging early and deliberately changes tactics, and continuously re-derives the highest-leverage remaining work from the scoreboard.

dimensions.name: Design revision under falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, data structures, or approach when a later feature (types, structs, ABI detail) exposes that an earlier design cannot support it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Compilers are notorious for early choices (untyped AST, ad-hoc register allocation, string-based codegen) that collapse under types/structs; the ability to recognize and refactor rather than pile hacks decides whether the tail of the task is reachable.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a broken design, piling special-cases and hacks even as failures compound.
anchors.3: Patches symptoms locally; resists structural change even when the same class of bug keeps recurring.
anchors.5: When an approach clearly fails, reworks the affected component and re-verifies rather than forcing it.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a limitation is architectural (not local), makes a deliberate refactor (e.g. adding type info through the AST/IR), and confirms the change unblocks the stuck feature class.
anchors.10: Proactively detects design strain before it becomes a wall, weighs refactor-vs-workaround explicitly, executes larger restructurings cleanly while protecting already-passing tests, and updates the plan/design record so the correction propagates instead of recurring.

dimensions.name: Compiler architecture & IR foresight
dimensions.description: Choosing pass boundaries and core data structures (AST/IR, symbol tables, type representation) with enough foresight to accommodate the full required feature set rather than painting into a corner.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike generic decomposition (what to do when) or adaptation (fixing after breakage), this is the upfront design judgment specific to compilers: a representation that anticipates types, structs, and the ABI avoids the most expensive class of rework on this task.

anchors.0: No deliberate architecture; monolithic, ad-hoc string-munging with no separable passes or reusable structures.
anchors.3: Minimal structure that works for the first trivial cases but has no provision for types, scopes, or layout.
anchors.5: Clean separation of lexer/parser/sema/codegen with data structures adequate for the early feature milestones.
anchors.8: Core representations (typed AST/IR, symbol/scope tables, type/layout model) are designed with the later hard features in mind, so structs/typedef/switch slot in without wholesale rewrites.
anchors.10: Architecture demonstrably anticipates the full contract — extensible IR and type system, clear invariants between passes — enabling most advanced features to be added additively; foresight is evidenced by later features landing cleanly rather than by luck.
